content.thinking:
I'm going through the claims one by one. The first two check out: the outage duration and the peak error rate both match what a reader would have seen. The third claim, about the legacy fallback being switched off as the trigger, is supported and I'm treating it as confirmed. I'm now checking the fourth claim, which says the change routed account pages through a newer path that likely breaks them.

I'm working through the remaining claims, and I'm counting the Argus response steps as supported. The first undo, of the monthly-spend-feature flag, didn't help, so that change was put back. The second, reverting the legacy-checkout-fallback change, is confirmed and still in place. The proposed fix to the newer code exists only as a draft and hasn't been shipped.

content.text:
I found nothing to flag. Each of the nine claims in the overview is backed by the record.

- **Duration, peak and cost:** these are given as named figures, so only the facts around them were checked.
- **Cause:** the sentence keeps "likely" where the record has it. The confirmed flag revert (C2/M2) supports blaming the fallback switch-off.
- **Nobody paged:** this matches the record's "none" for engineer time and its note that no on-call incident was linked.
- **The fix:** the postmortem says the Code-Fix Agent proposed it, and the ask's list credits it to Argus. So "Argus has proposed a fix" is fine. "Only a draft and has not been put into use" matches the record, which says it was opened as a draft and holds nothing after that.

supported.quote: For {duration}, shoppers' account pages on io-shop failed to load
rows: What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages failed to load

supported.quote: at the worst minute {peak_error_rate} of requests were failing

supported.quote: It started when an older fallback, legacy-checkout-fallback, was switched off.

That sent account pages through a newer way of building them, and the newer way likely breaks for any shopper who has bought nothing this month, because it divides by that month's number of purchases.
Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings.
rows: What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): 7,533.46 USD {customer_loss}

supported.quote: Nobody was paged, so the incident called no one away from other work.

No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one

supported.quote: Argus first undid the monthly-spend-feature flag, but that did not help, so Argus put it back.
Argus then undid the legacy-checkout-fallback change, turning the older fallback back on. That was confirmed to work and is still in place.
Argus has also proposed a fix to the newer code, but it is only a draft and has not been put into use.
rows: Argus: proposed a fix, PR #550 - opened as a draft
The fix it proposed: PR #550 ... opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.
